Subject: High tail latency on API during peering incident — request for SLA derate

Marcus / support team,

We observed significant tail latency affecting generation calls to text-api between ~07:50–09:20 PDT this morning. Error rate stayed low but 95/99th percentile latency spiked (see attached). Our engineers traced the path and saw packet loss toward CarrierX's peering fabric; CarrierX posted a short incident notice (attached).

CuraMed is requesting a formal uptime calculation adjustment for that window under the SLA — we believe it should be attributed as a third-party outage and qualify for partial derate/credit since the degradation affected >30% of our requests at the 99th percentile. Please confirm next steps and what additional evidence you need.

Attachments: curamed_latency_window_20250902.csv, carrierx_outage_notice_20250902.pdf

Thanks,
Sofia Ramos
Head of Platform, CuraMed
ops@curamed.com

Subject: Fwd: High tail latency on API during peering incident — internal evaluation

Folks — forwarding CuraMed's thread. Initial quick look: our edge telemetry shows elevated egress latency starting 07:48 PDT with packet retransmits consistent with CarrierX path degradation; service-side request acceptance and kernel-level timestamps show the router hop external to our VPC. However, some long-tail tokenization steps saw additional queuing — we need to quantify how much of the increased tail was due to Redwood queuing vs. network.

I think we should:
- Produce two ledgers: (1) raw availability by probe (what the customer observed) and (2) Redwood-service-attributable time (excluding clearly external carrier blips by IP/ASN).
- If the carrier blip drove >=25% of the observed 99th percentile increase for CuraMed's requests, recommend classification as third-party outage for credit purposes per SLA section 6.3.

Ben — can you pull packet-level traces and correlate with our flow logs? Neha — if we call this third-party, legal ops will need wording for the derate and whether to apply a pro-rated credit vs. one-time adjustment.

Marissa

Quick update from networking: I correlated CuraMed's client IP ranges to our egress flow logs and CarrierX ASN 64532 shows a sustained packet loss spike starting 07:47:22 PDT and persisting in bursts until ~09:10 PDT. During the highest-loss 20-minute sub-window (07:50–08:10 PDT) we see retransmit counts jump 4x; the Redwood runtime queuing contributed ~7–12ms median extra latency per request, but the carrier packet loss created >200ms extremes on affected flows.

My read: the dominant cause for 99th percentile spikes is CarrierX path loss. Based on SLA text (6.3), this looks like a third-party routing incident that should be excluded from Redwood-attributable uptime — customer should be eligible for a derate/credit.

I attached the packet correlation CSV.

Subject: Re: High tail latency on API during peering incident — request for SLA derate (decision and next steps)

Hi Sofia / CuraMed team — thanks for the patience. We completed the internal analysis and attached the calculation worksheet (summary below).

Summary of findings:
- Review window: 07:45–09:15 PDT on 2025-09-02 (UTC 14:45–16:15).
- Customer probe histogram included and reconciled with our edge traces (attached CSV).
- Attribution: CarrierX path loss accounted for ~82% of the observed 99th percentile increase across affected requests; Redwood queuing accounted for median 9ms additional latency and <10% of the tail delta.
- Determination: Per SLA 6.3 (third-party network events), we classify this as a third-party outage window eligible for a pro-rata derate.

Proposed remediation:
- Apply a one-time pro-rata credit equal to the expected monthly token charges for the affected request fraction (calculation attached).
- Credit will appear on the September invoice as a line item titled "CarrierX path derate — Sep 2 2025".
- We will provide a short statement for your auditors describing the attribution methodology.

Next actions (for internal workflow):
- Marcus: confirm credit amount with billing and schedule the invoice adjustment.
- Marissa: file an internal postmortem to see if we can reduce our contribution to tail latency during external carrier blips (low priority).

Sofia — let me know if the proposed remediation meets CuraMed's needs and we'll initiate the credit.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
